text: Your backswing is rushed. Take the club back slower and smoother.
meaning: The club goes back much faster than it should relative to the downswing.
wrong_motion: Backswing snatched up in a jerk, then the downswing.
correct_motion: Slow, even takeaway to the top (about 3x as long as the downswing), then accelerate down.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your downswing is quick relative to a slow backswing. Keep one smooth rhythm.
meaning: The backswing is slow but the downswing is a sudden lunge, so the rhythm breaks.
wrong_motion: Very slow backswing, pause, violent hit.
correct_motion: One continuous rhythm: smooth back, smooth acceleration through.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your lead arm is collapsing at the top. Keep it long and wide.
meaning: At the top of the backswing the lead arm (left for right-handers) bends at the elbow.
wrong_motion: Lead elbow folds at the top, hands close to the head.
correct_motion: Lead arm stays long and straight at the top, hands wide from the head.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your head is drifting sideways. Keep it centred over the ball until impact.
meaning: The head slides sideways away from the target during the backswing and back.
wrong_motion: Head drifts sideways with the shoulders.
correct_motion: Head stays centred over the ball while the shoulders turn around it.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are standing up through impact. Stay in your posture.
meaning: The head and chest rise before or at impact: losing posture.
wrong_motion: Torso straightens up through impact.
correct_motion: Spine angle held from address through impact.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are dipping down into the ball. Keep your height level.
meaning: The head drops toward the ball at impact.
wrong_motion: Knees and head sink down into the hit.
correct_motion: Height stays level through impact.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your hips slide away from the target. Turn around your trail hip instead of swaying.
meaning: The hips slide sideways away from the target in the backswing instead of rotating.
wrong_motion: Pelvis shifts sideways past the trail foot.
correct_motion: Hips rotate in place around the trail hip.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your shoulder turn is short. Rotate your back to the target.
meaning: The shoulders do not rotate far enough in the backswing.
wrong_motion: Arms lift the club with little shoulder rotation.
correct_motion: Shoulders rotate about 90 degrees so the back faces the target.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are finishing on your back foot. Get your weight onto your lead side.
meaning: At the finish the weight is still on the trail foot.
wrong_motion: Finish leaning back, weight on the trail foot.
correct_motion: Finish tall, belt buckle to the target, weight on the lead foot, trail heel up.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Use your legs. Dip and rise so the shot starts from the ground.
meaning: The shot uses only the arms; the legs do not dip and push.
wrong_motion: Straight legs, arms push the ball.
correct_motion: Knees dip, then extend so the legs start the shot and the arm finishes it.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are short-arming the release. Extend fully up through the ball.
meaning: The shooting arm stops short of straight at release.
wrong_motion: Elbow stays bent at release, ball pushed out.
correct_motion: Arm extends fully up toward the rim, wrist snaps.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your elbow is flaring out. Tuck it under the ball, in line with your shoulder.
meaning: At the set point the shooting elbow sticks out sideways.
wrong_motion: Elbow pointing out to the side under the ball.
correct_motion: Elbow tucked under the ball, in line with the shoulder and the rim.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are releasing low. Shoot up, not out, and finish high.
meaning: The ball leaves the hand low, around the face.
wrong_motion: Release at forehead height, flat push.
correct_motion: Release high above the head, arm up toward the rim.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your arm is finishing across your body. Finish straight toward the rim.
meaning: The shooting arm finishes angled across the body.
wrong_motion: Follow-through drifts across in front of the face.
correct_motion: Follow-through straight up toward the rim, in line with the shoulder.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Hold your follow-through until the ball reaches the rim.
meaning: The shooting hand drops right after release.
wrong_motion: Hand falls immediately after the ball leaves.
correct_motion: Hand held up, wrist relaxed down ('hand in the cookie jar') until the ball lands.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are drifting sideways. Go straight up and land where you took off.
meaning: The body moves sideways during the shot.
wrong_motion: Jumps and lands a step to the side.
correct_motion: Goes straight up and lands on the same spot.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your release is rushed after the dip. Let the legs finish first.
meaning: The arm releases before the legs finish pushing.
wrong_motion: Ball released while still crouched.
correct_motion: Legs extend first, ball released as the body reaches full height.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: There is a hitch between your dip and your release. Make it one motion.
meaning: There is a pause between the dip and the release.
wrong_motion: Dip, stop with ball at the forehead, then shoot.
correct_motion: Dip and shoot in one continuous motion.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Shoot with one hand. Keep your guide hand on the side of the ball and let only your shooting hand push it.
meaning: Both hands push the ball together instead of one shooting hand.
wrong_motion: Both hands behind the ball, both arms push forward like a chest pass.
correct_motion: Guide hand on the side of the ball, comes off at release; only the shooting arm extends.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Bend your knees more as you load. Power comes from the ground up.
meaning: The player stays upright while loading instead of bending the knees.
wrong_motion: Straight legs, swing from the arms.
correct_motion: Knees bend as the racket goes back, then the legs push up into the shot.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Reach up on your serve. Hit at full stretch above your hitting shoulder, not with a bent arm.
meaning: On the serve the hitting arm is bent at contact.
wrong_motion: Contact with a bent elbow at head height.
correct_motion: Contact at full stretch high above the hitting shoulder.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are meeting the ball too high. Let it drop into your strike zone.
meaning: The ball is struck too high (above the chest on a groundstroke).
wrong_motion: Swinging up at a ball at shoulder height.
correct_motion: Let the ball drop to between waist and chest height and hit there.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are meeting the ball too low. Get under it with your legs, or reach up fully on serve.
meaning: The ball is struck too low (or not at full reach on the serve).
wrong_motion: Reaching down at knee height with straight legs.
correct_motion: Bend the legs to get down to the ball; on serve reach fully up.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are cutting your swing short. Finish across your body.
meaning: The swing stops soon after contact.
wrong_motion: Racket stops at contact.
correct_motion: Racket swings through and finishes over the opposite shoulder.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Turn earlier and fully: by the end of your take-back your shoulders should be sideways, with your non-hitting shoulder pointing at the ball.
meaning: The shoulders stay facing the net during the take-back.
wrong_motion: Arm-only take-back, chest facing forward.
correct_motion: Early unit turn: shoulders rotate sideways as the racket goes back.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your head is moving through the hit. Keep your eyes at the contact point.
meaning: The head moves during the swing instead of staying at contact.
wrong_motion: Head turns to watch the target before contact.
correct_motion: Head still, eyes on the contact point until after the hit.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are snatching at the ball. Smooth acceleration beats a late rush.
meaning: The forward swing is a late, jerky rush.
wrong_motion: Racket held back then whipped forward abruptly.
correct_motion: Smooth, progressive acceleration from take-back to contact.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your forward swing is slow. Accelerate through contact.
meaning: The forward swing is slow and decelerates into the ball.
wrong_motion: Slow push at the ball.
correct_motion: Accelerate through contact.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Finish over your shoulder: keep swinging until the racket wraps up and over your opposite shoulder.
meaning: The swing stops low instead of finishing up and over the opposite shoulder.
wrong_motion: Racket stops at chest height in front of the body.
correct_motion: Racket wraps up and over the opposite shoulder, hitting elbow high.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Finish with your hitting elbow up at nose height, pointing toward your target.
meaning: At the finish the hitting elbow is below the face.
wrong_motion: Elbow finishes down by the chest.
correct_motion: Elbow finishes up at nose height, pointing toward the target.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Use your other hand: reach it out toward the ball as you turn, to judge the space between you and the ball.
meaning: The non-hitting hand stays tucked in during the turn, so the spacing to the ball is guessed.
wrong_motion: Free hand stays by the body as the racket goes back.
correct_motion: Free hand reaches out toward the incoming ball during the turn, then releases before contact.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You're jammed: give yourself more room between your body and the ball.
meaning: The ball is too close to the body at contact.
wrong_motion: Elbow jammed into the side at contact.
correct_motion: An arm's length of space between body and contact point.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You're reaching for the ball: move your feet so it comes to you.
meaning: The player reaches for a ball that is too far away.
wrong_motion: Arm over-reaching, body leaning away from the ball.
correct_motion: Feet move so contact happens at a comfortable arm's length.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Make contact further in front of you, out ahead of your front foot.
meaning: Contact happens beside or behind the body instead of out in front.
wrong_motion: Ball hit level with the hips.
correct_motion: Ball hit in front of the front foot.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Extend out toward your target through contact before wrapping to the finish.
meaning: The racket wraps around the body straight after contact.
wrong_motion: Hand pulls across the body immediately after contact.
correct_motion: Hand extends out toward the target first, then wraps to the finish.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Load your back leg on the take-back: sit your weight over your back foot.
meaning: Weight stays on the front foot during the take-back.
wrong_motion: Hips over the front foot as the racket goes back.
correct_motion: Hips sit over the back foot, back knee bent, as the racket goes back.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Push off your back leg and move your weight onto your front leg through contact.
meaning: Weight stays back through contact.
wrong_motion: Hips stay over the back foot at contact.
correct_motion: Hips move from the back foot onto the front foot through contact.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Fully extend your hitting arm at contact on the backhand and serve.
meaning: On the backhand or serve the hitting arm is bent at contact.
wrong_motion: Contact with a bent elbow.
correct_motion: Contact with the hitting arm fully extended.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Stay lower. Bend your knees instead of bending at the waist.
meaning: The player stands too tall instead of staying low.
wrong_motion: Upright, bending only at the waist to reach low balls.
correct_motion: Athletic stance: knees bent, back fairly upright, paddle in front.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your paddle is dropping between shots. Keep it up at chest height.
meaning: Between shots the paddle hangs low by the knees.
wrong_motion: Paddle drops below the waist between shots.
correct_motion: Paddle up in front at chest height between shots.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Your backswing is too big. Keep the paddle in front of your body.
meaning: The paddle goes far back behind the body before the shot.
wrong_motion: Big tennis-style take-back behind the hip.
correct_motion: Compact take-back: paddle stays in front of the body.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Reach up on your overhead. Hit at full stretch above your hitting shoulder, not with a bent arm.
meaning: On an overhead the hitting arm is bent at contact.
wrong_motion: Overhead hit with a bent elbow at head height.
correct_motion: Overhead hit at full stretch above the hitting shoulder.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are reaching up for balls you could let drop.
meaning: Balls are hit too high instead of letting them drop.
wrong_motion: Reaching up to hit at shoulder height.
correct_motion: Let the ball drop and hit around waist height.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are hitting from too low. Bend and lift with your legs.
meaning: Low balls are reached for by bending over instead of using the legs.
wrong_motion: Bending at the waist to reach a low ball.
correct_motion: Bend the knees to get down, then lift through the ball.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: You are stabbing at the ball. Push through toward your target.
meaning: The stroke is a short jab with no follow-through.
wrong_motion: Paddle jabs at the ball and stops.
correct_motion: Paddle pushes through toward the target and finishes there.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side

text: Keep your head still and watch the ball onto the paddle.
meaning: The head moves during the stroke.
wrong_motion: Head turns to watch the target before contact.
correct_motion: Head still, eyes on the paddle at contact.
hand: shooting/hitting arm is the dominant side; golf lead arm is the non-dominant side
